details: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance confirmed a $6.4 billion hack on October 29, with blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis attributing the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor cybercrime group. Binance is working to resume withdrawals and has reportedly frozen approximately $3 billion of the stolen assets, with an additional $6.34 billion prepared to cover losses. This incident has led to renewed selling pressure on Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, institutional outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs, and a "Fear" sentiment in the crypto market's Fear and Greed Index.
title: Binance Hack Spurs Market Jitters, Billions Frozen

details: In the wake of the Binance hack, the global crypto market capitalization stands at $2.7 trillion, seeing a slight uptick of 0.5% on October 31st. However, the Fear and Greed Index remains at 30, indicating "Fear" among investors. Bitcoin is currently trading around $77,367, up 0.6% in the last 24 hours but continues to face overall selling pressure and is testing key support levels. Ethereum has shown a 2.2% increase to $2,241, leading some major coins. Gaming Blockchains and the Optimism Superchain Ecosystem were notable gainers, while Bitway experienced a significant decline.
title: Crypto Markets Volatile Post-Binance Hack, Bitcoin Tests Support

details: Ripple's Swell 2026 conference concluded with several announcements aimed at fostering institutional adoption. Coinbase expanded access for Ripple's stablecoin, RLUSD, across its platforms, and Ripple announced a broader partnership with Robinhood. Additionally, BNY Mellon expanded custody support for both XRP and RLUSD, with Moody's assigning investment-grade ratings to RLUSD. Despite these positive developments for Ripple's enterprise solutions, the XRP token's price experienced a slump, reaching new local lows.
title: Ripple's Swell 2026 Boosts RLUSD Adoption, XRP Price Dips
